intended: All four runs are titanium at Kestrel Works on the night shift inside one quarter, so one retooling covers every case at once. The mid-passage line records that "Every shop refitted its machines with a faster insert grade that quarter" and that "every logged run was cut on one of those machines", so the refit reached all four runs. A change of insert grade moves cycle time by itself, and each run is compared against the same run last quarter, when the older grade was still fitted, rather than against a run on the same inserts over the same period. The 4 to 7 minute reductions cannot be separated from the retooling.
reported: A named alternative cause reaches every unit: "Every shop refitted its machines with a faster insert grade that quarter, and every logged run was cut on one of those machines." A faster insert grade shortens cycle time on its own, so the 4-7 minute reductions cannot be attributed to the coolant.

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the averages over the patients who were reassessed at the follow-up clinic, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of each intake missed that clinic. The claim is about the protocol restoring shoulder range of motion for the patients put on it, so the population is the whole intake and the register covers three quarters of it. Patients whose shoulders are not improving are the ones who stop turning up for reassessment, so the missing quarter is where the flat and negative results would sit, and the reported degrees are an average over the patients who came back. All four intakes are rotator cuff cases on the Marbeck ward in one spring and each loses the same quarter, so no case in the register measures the patients the others missed.
reported: The abduction averages "cover the patients who were reassessed at the follow-up clinic" while "a quarter of each intake missed the follow-up clinic", so the 9-16 degree gains describe only the three-quarters who returned, and poor responders are exactly the ones likeliest to be missing. The corticosteroid confound is ruled out because "every intake was medically barred from receiving them".

intended: In cases one and three the yield was measured before the drip line was fitted: 18 June precedes 3 August at Hollow Ridge, and 17 March precedes 2 May at Bellamy Flats. Half the evidence therefore describes yield that was already in hand when the line went in, so it cannot be evidence for the line. The two remaining cases, Netley Downs and Corradine Estate, are not enough on their own.
reported: In two of the four blocks the measured gain predates the intervention: Hollow Ridge was 'fitted 3 August' but the 0.6 t/ha gain is recorded 'by 18 June', and Bellamy Flats was 'fitted 2 May' but the 0.7 t/ha gain is recorded 'by 17 March'. The other two blocks (fitted 8 December / by 23 February; fitted 7 September / by 22 November) run forward on a consistent ~2.5 month lag, so cases One and Three have measurement dates falling before the drip line existed.

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the purchase counts over the sessions that signed in, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of each segment never signed in. The claim is about the new checkout page raising purchases for the segment, so the numbers describe three quarters of the population the claim is about. Signed-in shoppers arrive with saved cards and addresses and convert at different rates from guests, so the uncounted quarter cannot be assumed to have moved with the counted part. All four segments are desktop sessions from Canada via search inside March and each carries the same sign-in gap, so no case in the log supplies what the others leave out.
reported: The purchase counts "cover the sessions that signed in, and a quarter of each segment never signed in", so the measured population is a quarter narrower than the claim's population and the checkout page itself could change who signs in. (The site-wide discount is neutralized, since "every segment browsed a fixed-price contract catalogue".)

intended: The mid-passage line tallies the infection rates over the patients discharged from each ward, and the clause beside it records that each ward transferred out a quarter of those admitted. The claim is about ward infection rates, which is a claim about everyone the ward admitted, so a quarter of that population sits outside the numbers entirely. Patients who deteriorate are the ones moved to intensive care or to another hospital, and infection is a common reason for that move, so the excluded quarter is precisely where infections would concentrate and the reported drop is measured over the patients who did well enough to leave by the front door. The four entries span four hospitals, four ward types, four quarters and four auditors, and the transfer-out clause applies at each ward, so every case is missing the same quarter of its own population.
reported: The denominator is narrower than the claim: "Rates cover the patients discharged from each ward, and each ward transferred out a quarter of those admitted." A quarter of admitted patients - plausibly the sickest, most infection-prone ones - are excluded from the ward infection rate entirely.
